structure: Part 4, Origin, reason for import and hub. Read in full, by line range in backlog.json, the eight in-scope rows of this slice: inc-079 (3096-3376, origin, done, region of origin code prefix), inc-067 (9817-10221, import-reason, done, purpose and exit questions as conditional reveals), inc-069 (10417-10643, hub, done, Exit details task), inc-081 (10644-10788, origin, blocked, Canary Islands / Jersey / French Guiana in the country list), inc-082 (10789-10933, origin, done, origin page refuses to save), inc-071 (12632-12915, import-reason, blocked, port of exit list), inc-033 (28474-28610, hub, done, Commodity details task row) and inc-043 (30082-30186, hub, rejected, 'Notification tasklist' heading). Each row carries title, detail, finding {frontend, prototype, difference, correction, falsifiedBy, relatedTo}, citations, provenance and PRs; the judgement fields are openQuestions (inc-079: 1, inc-067: 3, inc-033: 1), notes (inc-067: two failed attempts, inc-043: falsified attempt), failure_reason (inc-069, inc-082: both cleared false main-red stops) and decision (inc-081, inc-071: block on MDM; inc-043: falsified). Claims record, per row, what DR1 judged (built, blocked, rejected), then every deferral, open question, action and reason in those judgement fields; where a done row's finding also leaves a point to settle (inc-079's reference-data route) or a blocked row leaves its finding's question open (inc-081's EFTA states, inc-071's V4 spec conflict), that is recorded as a gap. Provenance matching notes, citations, evidence, screens and PR bookkeeping were read for context and not claimed.

claims.statement: DR1 parity built (status done) the region of origin code as a fixed prefix derived from the chosen country of origin, with the user entering only the part after the prefix.
claims.quote: Design release 1 fills in the country's code as a fixed prefix and asks only for the rest of the region of origin code; Frontend makes the user type the whole code inside five characters.
claims.note: status "done", commit 7f2c45ab, frontend PR #216 and tests PR #135 merged.

claims.statement: As built in DR1 parity, the region of origin code prefix is rendered server-side only, from the stored answers, so on a first visit before the page is submitted the prefix is not shown and the user sees a bare five-character box.
claims.quote: This increment renders the prefix server-side only: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:169 sets regionCodePrefix = prefixFor(values.countryOfOrigin), and the GET path at controller.js:172-175 feeds those values from the stored answers, so on a first visit — a user starting a notification, choosing France and checking Yes without submitting — regionCodePrefix is '' and govuk-frontend drops the prefix element entirely (its input template's hasPrefix guard). The user sees a bare five-character box

claims.statement: On that first pass a user who types the whole code, such as 'FR-DUB', is rejected with the error 'Region of origin code must be 5 characters or less'.
claims.quote: may type the whole code ('FR-DUB'), and is rejected by maxText('regionOfOriginCodeSuffix', 5) with 'Region of origin code must be 5 characters or less'.

claims.statement: Nothing is stored wrongly in that case: the submit derives the prefix from the submitted country, and the error re-render then shows the prefix.
claims.quote: Nothing is stored wrong — the POST derives the prefix from the payload's country (controller.js:80-97) and the error re-render then shows the prefix — but the first pass does not yet deliver the design's point that the user cannot get the prefix wrong.

claims.statement: Design release 1 writes the region code prefix from client-side script the moment a country is chosen, with no form submission; DR1 parity DEFERRED building that live prefix rather than fixing it in the increment.
claims.quote: Design release 1 writes the prefix from client-side JS the moment a country is chosen (workareas/shared/dr1c-parity/specs/prototype/consignment.pw.js:146-153 records that the ISO prefix is written by the country search, not by the radio, and asserts the prefix reads 'FR' with no form submission). DEFERRED rather than fixed in this increment because code alone cannot settle it

claims.statement: A live prefix needs a new progressive-enhancement client component rather than a server change.
claims.quote: (1) it needs a new progressive-enhancement client component under src/client/javascripts/components/ registered in application.js, not a server change

claims.statement: Undecided: what the region code prefix shows before a country is chosen, because govukInput cannot render an empty prefix box. The options named are an empty grey box, a hidden element the script reveals, or hand-rolled markup, and hand-rolling departs from the govuk-frontend toolbox.
claims.quote: (2) govukInput cannot render an empty prefix box, so someone has to decide what the prefix shows before a country is chosen — an empty grey box, a hidden element the script reveals, or hand-rolled markup outside the govuk macro, and hand-rolling departs from the govuk-frontend toolbox this repo holds to

claims.statement: Undecided: the no-JavaScript behaviour of the region code prefix; it stays as shipped (server-side prefix after submit) until decided.
claims.quote: (3) the no-JS behaviour has to be decided, and stays as shipped here

claims.statement: The live prefix depends on the country of origin control (inc-077), which may be replaced by an accessible autocomplete and so change what the prefix script listens to.
claims.quote: (4) this increment's own relatedTo already ties the prefix to inc-077 ('the prefix is derived from the country of origin, so this change depends on the country control being able to report the chosen country'), which may replace the plain select with the accessible autocomplete and so change what the component listens to.

claims.statement: Open action: decide with design whether the live region code prefix is required for Design release 1 parity, and if it is, build it together with the country control change in inc-077.
claims.quote: ACTION: decide with design whether the live prefix is required for Design release 1 parity, and if it is, build it with inc-077 so the country control and its prefix listener land together.

claims.statement: The row's finding left one point to settle: whether the region code prefix is rebuilt from the country option values (needing no new reference data) or lifted from Design release 1's prefix table, which is keyed on its own country labels and so rides on the country list change in inc-081 (since blocked).
claims.quote: How much reference data this needs is the one point the two runs read differently. Frontend already holds the two-letter code as the value of every country option (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:57-61), and Design release 1's own prefix map departs from the plain country code only for Ceuta and Melilla, neither of which is in Frontend's list — on that reading nothing new is needed. Against that, Design release 1's prefix table is keyed on its own country label strings, so if the prefix map is lifted across rather than rebuilt from the option values, this change rides on the country list change in inc-081. Settle which of those two routes is being taken before starting.
claims.note: Sits in finding.difference, not openQuestions; the row is done, and the row does not record which route was taken. Recorded as a gap because inc-081 is blocked (claim p4-030).

claims.statement: The first build attempt of the conditional-reveals change (2026-09-06) failed on the E2E leg because the backend container could not reach Mongo; it was assessed as an environment fault, not a defect in the diff.
claims.ref: backlog.json inc-067, notes, first ATTEMPT FAILED
claims.quote: ATTEMPT FAILED (2026-09-06) — red verification ladder, work preserved but NOT built. What went red: the tests-repo E2E leg (playwright.docker-compose.config.ts against the workspace stack) could not run. Assessment: environment fault rather than a defect proven in the diff, but unproven either way — needs a healthy stack, or CI, to re-run the ladder.

claims.statement: After the reveal move, none of the four conditional-reveal answers on the import reason page (purpose, destination country, port of exit, exit date) is proven to work without JavaScript: the only no-JS test of the exit date field was deleted with its page and nothing replaced it.

claims.quote: because the questions no longer have pages of their own there is no other route to them: if govuk-frontend's gating of .govuk-radios__conditional--hidden behind .govuk-frontend-supported ever regresses, every follow-up question becomes permanently unreachable for no-JS users with nothing in the suite failing.

claims.statement: Lighthouse coverage of the reveal states was DEFERRED because it needs a redesign of the Lighthouse harness (one route audited under several notification shapes, plus opening a reveal before the audit).
claims.quote: the alternative — auditing the same route under more than one notification shape — is a structural change to FILLED_BY, auditUrls and reportNames, which today assume one shape per path and one report name per route, plus a way to open a reveal before the audit runs. That is a Lighthouse-harness redesign, not a fix to this diff.

claims.statement: Open action: decide with the team whether reveal-state accessibility is audited by Lighthouse or left to the fit-spec axe scans, which do scan with a reveal open; if Lighthouse, let a route be audited under several shapes with distinguishing report names.
claims.quote: ACTION: decide with the team whether reveal-state accessibility is audited by Lighthouse or left to the fit-spec axe runs in import-reason.fit.spec.js (which do scan with a reveal open). claims.statement: After the reveal move, the opening run's rule that a step whose gate is closed is skipped and the next reachable step is shown is no longer pinned by any test, and no real combination of answers can currently reach it.
claims.quote: the continue branch at run.js:44-49 — documented at run.js:15-20 as 'a null target skips the step' — is unpinned. ... so no combination of real answers gates one step off while a later one passes — the skip is currently unreachable through data.

claims.statement: Pinning the skip rule was DEFERRED because it needs either a production change to accept an injectable step list or module mocking of the gates, which the repo does not do in app code.
claims.quote: DEFERRED rather than fixed in this increment because there is no honest way to pin it without expanding the blast radius. ... Pinning it therefore needs either a production change to run.js to accept an injectable step list, or module mocking of flow/gates.js, a technique this repo confines to infrastructure boundaries (auth, plugins, helpers) and never uses anywhere under src/server/app.

claims.statement: Open action: decide how the flow layer pins branches no real answer state can reach: (a) accept the gap until a gated run step returns, (b) let the run take its steps as a parameter, or (c) sanction mocking the gates; whichever is chosen, add a test 'Should skip a run step whose gate is closed and land on the next reachable one'.
claims.quote: ACTION: decide how the flow layer pins branches that no real answer state can reach. Either (a) accept the gap until an increment reintroduces a conditionally-gated RUN_STEP and require that increment to pin the skip with real answers, or (b) agree that flow/run.js may take its steps as a parameter (export nextRunTarget(stepId, scope, journeyId, steps = RUN_STEPS)) so run.test.js can drive a two-step list whose first target is null, or (c) sanction vi.mock of flow/gates.js inside src/server/app tests. Whichever is chosen, add the test named for the behaviour: 'Should skip a run step whose gate is closed and land on the next reachable one'.
